findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the exact model id (and region if different) used to generate ticket digests for candidate 2, so the digest text and its recall are reproducible.
evidence: 'Trivial model class, one call per ticket, cached in the fixture directory keyed by content hash.'
The vector candidate names an exact model id (amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0) but the digest candidate names only a 'Trivial model class'.
findings.finding: The digest candidate (candidate 2) names the prompt text, contract, and pinned source commit, but does not name the LLM model/model-class actually used to produce the digests. 'Trivial model class, one call per ticket' leaves the executor to choose the model id.
scenarios: Executor must pick a Bedrock/LLM model for digest generation with no stated default, risking non-reproducible digests between runs.
findings.suggested_fix: Name a concrete Bedrock model id for the digest 'trivial model class' (e.g. the project's configured small/cheap model), mirroring how the vector candidate pins amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm (or route to a credential/entitlement spike) that `amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0` is permitted under the Bedrock IAM policy, which infra/runbooks/bedrock-access.md documents as scoped to `anthropic.claude-*` only, before committing to the Titan `invoke_model` vector candidate; state the auth precondition in the plan.
evidence: Plan: 'embeddings of an LLM summary ... from Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2, model id amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0, called with the boto3 bedrock-runtime client's invoke_model'

infra/runbooks/bedrock-access.md:122-129: negative control repeats with `--model-id amazon.nova-pro-v1:0` expecting `AccessDeniedException ... not authorized to perform: bedrock:InvokeModel ... amazon.nova-pro-v1:0`, with the note 'the policy is meant to permit anthropic.claude-* only'

Repo search for `invoke_model` / `inputText` / `titan-embed` in source returned no call-path matches: the only Bedrock use is pydantic-ai's BedrockProvider for Claude TEXT generation (src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py), so the Titan embeddings endpoint is a NEW, previously-unused surface
Evidence class: Contradicted — the documented IAM scope (`anthropic.claude-*` only) falsifies an `amazon.titan-*` InvokeModel call under current entitlements
findings.finding: The vector candidate depends on calling Bedrock model id `amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0` via `bedrock:InvokeModel`, but the documented Bedrock IAM policy is scoped to `anthropic.claude-*` only and its negative control proves a non-Claude model id returns AccessDeniedException on bedrock:InvokeModel — so the Titan embeddings call would be DENIED under current entitlements, and the plan neither states this auth precondition nor routes the gap to a spike.
findings.location: Approach → candidate 3 (Vector: Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2)
scenarios: measure.py --candidate vector runs against real Bedrock credentials in the gerrit-instance-role environment and every invoke_model call fails with AccessDeniedException, producing no vector recall numbers for the ADR
findings.suggested_fix: Add an auth precondition to candidate 3 naming the IAM action (`bedrock:InvokeModel` on `arn:aws:bedrock:...::foundation-model/amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0`) and either verify the policy already grants it or scope a SPIKE to extend the `anthropic.claude-*`-only policy to the Titan embeddings model before the full build.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Have the ADR specify the full lifecycle of the shared index/cache: a retire/cleanup path (eviction of stale entries) and a concurrency discipline (lock/transaction or single-writer ownership) for the reader-process incremental catch-up update.
evidence: "cached in the fixture directory keyed by content hash" — no eviction/retire path stated
"the catch-up rule (reader-process incremental update from `git diff --name-only <indexed_sha> <head>`...)"
ABSENCE: no statement of how concurrent reader processes coordinate when both update the shared `.git/rebar/similar.sqlite`, and no cleanup for cache entries whose tickets no longer exist
findings.finding: The plan introduces persistent shared state — the content-hash-keyed cache in the fixture directory and the ADR-recommended `.git/rebar/similar.sqlite` index with a reader-process incremental catch-up update — but specifies no RETIRE/cleanup path (the cache accumulates entries for deleted/renamed tickets indefinitely) and no concurrency discipline for the UPDATE step: two reader processes each applying `git diff` incremental updates to the one shared SQLite index is a check-then-act race with no lock/transaction stated.
findings.location: Approach (digest cache); ADR content — index path, freshness key, and catch-up rule
findings.suggested_fix: Record in the ADR that the incremental update runs inside a SQLite transaction under an advisory lock (or single-writer rebuild), and that stale cache/index rows for deleted tickets are pruned on update.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the parent's named '51-pair' benchmark with the leaf's re-derived, stratified benchmark: update parent epic 62dc AC1 / child decomposition to describe the re-derived, SHA-pinned, lexical/semantic-stratified set (semantic stratum as decision criterion) so the leaf is a faithful subset of the parent's written contract.
evidence: Parent AC1: 'measured recall@5 and recall@10 on the 51-pair duplicate benchmark built from the store'
Parent child decomposition: 'Research and design (first child...): builds the 51-pair benchmark, measures the candidate architectures, writes the ADR. Delivers criterion 1.'
Parent measured facts: 'of 51 known duplicate pairs in the store, 44 are semantic rather than lexical'
Leaf: '482 recorded duplicates links close into 148 clusters ... enumerating to 1,524 within-cluster pairs'; '93 pairs have differing titles. Those are the semantic set, and they are the benchmark'

The leaf re-derives via the same method the parent's facts describe (recorded duplicates links -> transitive closure -> within-cluster pairs) and justifies departing from 51 with the bulk-creation artifact, so this is refinement, not a contradiction of the parent's goal
findings.finding: The leaf redefines the parent's named '51-pair duplicate benchmark' deliverable: it re-derives the pair set at a newer pinned tickets-branch SHA (1,524 total within-cluster pairs) and designates the 93 differing-title pairs as the decision benchmark under a lexical/semantic stratification, where the parent's AC1, child decomposition, and measured-facts all name a '51-pair' benchmark. The re-derivation is well-justified and consistent with the parent's underlying goal, but the parent's as-written contract still says '51 pairs', so the two should be reconciled.
findings.location: Plan 'Context / Problem' and 'Approach' vs parent epic 62dc AC1 / child decomposition
scenarios: A reviewer or sibling child reads parent AC1 expecting a 51-pair benchmark and finds a 1,524-pair re-derivation with a 93-pair semantic decision set
Parent AC1 verification ('the ADR exists ... with the numbers and the benchmark command') is checked against the stale '51-pair' wording
findings.suggested_fix: Update parent 62dc AC1 and its child-decomposition line to drop the fixed '51-pair' count in favor of 'a duplicate benchmark re-derived at a pinned tickets-branch SHA, stratified into lexical and semantic pairs, with the semantic stratum as the decision criterion'; this stales the parent's plan-review attestation and forces its re-review, after which the leaf aligns cleanly.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify timeout + retry/backoff (and surfacing, not swallowing) for the per-ticket digest LLM call and the Titan `invoke_model` call, so a transient throttle/5xx during the ~630-ticket pass is recovered rather than aborting the run.
evidence: "called with the boto3 `bedrock-runtime` client's `invoke_model`"
"one call per ticket, cached in the fixture directory keyed by content hash"
Testing only covers: "the runner skips a candidate cleanly when Bedrock credentials are absent and says so" — no mention of timeout/retry/transient-throttle on the live calls
ABSENCE: no timeout or retry/backoff is specified for either the per-ticket digest call or the per-ticket Titan embed call
findings.finding: The plan adds live external calls — Titan `invoke_model` over bedrock-runtime and one `ticket_digest` LLM call per ticket (~630) — but specifies error handling only for the credentials-absent case (skip the candidate). It states no timeout, retry/backoff, or handling of transient throttle/5xx (e.g. a Bedrock 429 mid-run), so a single transient failure part-way through a 630-ticket embedding/summarization pass can abort the measurement with no recovery, forcing a full re-run.
findings.suggested_fix: State a per-call timeout and bounded retry-with-backoff on transient Bedrock errors (429/5xx), and that the content-hash cache lets an aborted pass resume without re-charging completed tickets.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the candidate corpus explicitly: either draw candidates from the full live store (or a representative sample of non-duplicate distractors) so recall@k reflects production retrieval, or justify in the plan/ADR why a 630-ticket all-duplicate pool is a sound proxy and bound the inflation.
evidence: Plan: candidate 1 is 'SQLite FTS5 ... in a temporary index built from the fixture'; candidate 3 says '630 normalized vectors need no ANN library' — i.e. the candidate pool is the 630 fixture tickets
Plan stores description heads 'per ticket' only for clustered tickets (630 over 148 clusters)

In the fixture corpus every ticket is a member of some duplicate cluster, so a query's true match is always present among a small, pre-filtered, all-related pool — unlike production retrieval over ~5,663 tickets that are overwhelmingly non-duplicates
Prior art ADR 0086 explicitly reported recall 'STABLE from a 60- to a 200-ticket corpus' (docs/adr/0086-cross-ticket-overlap.md:41), establishing corpus size/composition as a material, known variable
findings.finding: The retrieval candidates are measured against a corpus consisting only of the 630 clustered (all-duplicate) tickets stored in the fixture, not against the whole live store the production feature must search, so recall@5/@10 will be inflated and may not transfer to the real task.
findings.location: Approach, candidates 1-3 ('a temporary index built from the fixture'; 'Store ... per ticket in evals/similar-tickets/benchmark.json'); Scope (benchmark.json stores only cluster tickets)
scenarios: A candidate that near-saturates recall on the 630-ticket all-duplicate pool but collapses when the true match must be surfaced from thousands of unrelated tickets
The ADR picks an architecture on numbers that do not describe the deployed retrieval task
findings.suggested_fix: Add non-duplicate distractor tickets to the candidate index (e.g. the full live store or a sampled subset), and record the corpus size/composition in the fixture header; report recall@k against that corpus, not against the 630 clustered tickets alone.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Report the per-stratum recall with its sample size and an uncertainty measure (e.g. a binomial confidence interval or per-pair win/loss breakdown across candidates), and state in the ADR how a close result is adjudicated given N=93.
evidence: Plan: the semantic benchmark is 93 pairs; a single pair is ~1.08% of recall
Plan reports recall@5 and recall@10 as the deciding figures but never mentions confidence intervals, significance, or power across the three candidates
On N=93 a few pairs' difference between candidates can be within noise, yet the ADR must 'name one architecture and justify it from the semantic stratum'
findings.finding: The decision criterion — the semantic stratum — is only 93 pairs, and the plan reports point recall@5/@10 per candidate without any statistical-power or confidence-interval treatment, so small-N noise could drive the architecture choice.
findings.location: Context ('93 pairs have differing titles ... Those are the semantic set, and they are the benchmark') and Approach ('Report recall@5 and recall@10 per stratum ... with the semantic stratum as the decision criterion')
scenarios: Vector beats digest by 3-4 pairs on 93 and is declared the winner when the difference is not statistically distinguishable
A re-derivation at a later SHA shifts the 93-pair set and flips the ordering

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the fallback for a failed/empty per-ticket digest LLM call (retry/backoff, or skip-and-report-count) so a partial digest-generation failure cannot silently bias candidate 2/3 per-stratum recall.
evidence: Plan specifies only the Bedrock-credentials-absent fallback: 'the runner skips a candidate cleanly when Bedrock credentials are absent and says so'
Candidate 2: 'one call per ticket, cached in the fixture directory keyed by content hash' — no handling for a call that errors or returns empty
Candidate 3 reuses 'the same digest text', so a missing digest also breaks the vector candidate
ABSENCE: the plan has no rule for a ticket whose digest call fails/returns empty (retry, skip-with-count, abort)
findings.finding: No fallback is specified for a per-ticket digest LLM call that fails or returns empty/malformed output, even though candidates 2 and 3 both require a digest for every one of the 630 tickets.
scenarios: A transient model error or empty completion on a subset of 630 tickets leaves some tickets with no digest, silently shrinking the effective corpus and biasing per-stratum recall@5/@10 without any surfaced signal
